doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Learning publicity: English major and instinct
summary: Jacobs studied English and learned publicity instinctively, trusted by the artists she worked with.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you have education or training for some of the things that you ended up doing, being a publicist and a promoter and all those kinds of things, or did you learn on the job?

My uncle was a very, very clever man and very, very good. And he gave me a lot of freedom. You know he just let me do it. And I guess I just did it. But of course I did have an education, I majored in English, I primarily wanted to be a journalist or a librarian, and as far as publicity went I just kind of instinctively knew that you had to get a message to people and I thought about the best way to do it. And I’ve made some mistakes but generally speaking I think I was very successful because the people that I worked with trusted me. I couldn’t fail them.
